listings.detail: Program hosted at Constellation's Berkeley research center, pairing emerging talent with senior advisors on alignment research, governance, and strategy projects. Fellows receive mentorship and career support.

listings.title: Constellation Visiting Fellows
listings.detail: Lightly structured program for people working full-time on AI safety to continue their work from Constellation's research center in Berkeley. During that time fellows connect with leading researchers and find collaborators.

listings.title: GovAI Fellowship
listings.detail: Governance program run by the Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI), aimed at early-career individuals and established professionals new to AI governance. Participants pursue a research or applied project under expert mentorship and build field connections.

listings.title: ARENA (Alignment Research Engineer Accelerator)
listings.detail: Trains aspiring alignment researchers and engineers in ML through an intensive curriculum. Participants work through programming exercises in pairs under the guidance of expert teaching assistants.

listings.title: Generator Residency
listings.detail: Program run by Kairos and Constellation for AI safety generalists. Residents start a new project or join an organization, with mentorship and help landing full-time roles.

listings.title: Gen Stream
listings.detail: For generalists moving into AI safety. Participants build a project sourced from an AI safety org, with talks, red teaming, and mentor 1-1s – ending with a demo day.

listings.title: Global Challenges Project (GCP)
listings.detail: Intensive residential workshop run by Kairos, exploring the foundational arguments around risks from advanced AI and biotechnology. Includes guest speakers, career planning, and 1-on-1s.

listings.title: ERA:AI Fellowship
listings.detail: Research program for researchers and entrepreneurs mitigating risks from frontier AI. Fellows pursue a mentored project in technical AI safety, AI governance, or technical AI governance.

listings.title: LASR Labs
listings.detail: Research program focused on reducing the risk of loss of control to advanced AI, tackling action-relevant questions on concrete threat models. Participants work in teams of 3–4 with an experienced supervisor to write an academic-style paper.

listings.title: Pivotal AI Safety Fellowship
listings.detail: Program for projects spanning technical AI safety, governance, and AI-bio. Includes mentorship, research management, workshops, and workspace at the London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA). Provides continued funding of up to six months for strong work.

listings.title: AI Governance Taskforce
listings.detail: Helps experienced professionals transition into AI governance careers. Small teams tackle policy-relevant research with expert partners like the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) and GovAI, typically producing a paper and a policy brief or article.

listings.title: Algoverse AI Safety
listings.detail: Immerses participants in safety research through expert-led sessions and hands-on projects. Teams of three survey research agendas, build technical skills, and work with mentors to produce a paper for conference submission.

listings.title: ARBOx (Alignment Research Bootcamp Oxford)
listings.detail: Intensive run by the Oxford AI Safety Initiative (OAISI) designed to rapidly build AI safety skills – covering interpretability, RLHF, and replicating alignment research papers. Expects basic familiarity with linear algebra, Python, and AI safety.

listings.title: CAMBRIA
listings.detail: ML upskilling program from the Cambridge Boston Alignment Initiative (CBAI) for aspiring technical AI safety researchers. Covers mechanistic interpretability and reinforcement learning via the ARENA curriculum.

listings.title: CBAI Research Fellowship
listings.detail: Research program run by the Cambridge Boston Alignment Initiative (CBAI). Fellows work closely with mentors on projects across interpretability, formal verification, and AI governance.

listings.title: MARS (Mentorship for Alignment Research Students)
listings.detail: Research program from the Cambridge AI Safety Hub (CAISH), pairing teams of 2–4 with mentors on technical alignment and governance research. A one-week in-person kickoff leads into 8–10 weeks of remote work.

listings.title: Cooperative AI Summer School
listings.detail: Intensive program for early-career professionals already working in or studying cooperative AI. Participants attend talks from researchers, work on collaborative projects tackling cooperative AI challenges, and receive career guidance and mentoring. Run by CAIF.

listings.title: Introduction to Cooperative AI
listings.detail: Aims to deepen participants' understanding of the field of cooperative AI and help them prepare to contribute. Includes weekly exercises, group discussions facilitated by field practitioners, and a dedicated community. Run by Cooperative AI Foundation (CAIF).

listings.title: LASST Summer Fellowship
listings.detail: Program by Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology (LASST) for law students and attorneys. Fellows research legal and regulatory issues in AI governance and advanced technology, and write a white paper or memo.

listings.title: National Security Law and AI
listings.detail: Course by the Vista Institute for AI Policy for staffers, policy professionals, researchers, and recent graduates. Expert-led sessions cover export controls, military applications of AI, and securing model weights.

listings.title: AI Agents and the Law
listings.detail: Course by the Vista Institute for AI Policy on how the law applies to increasingly capable AI agents. An introductory module covers technical and legal foundations, then research streams lead to a research proposal.

listings.title: XLab Summer Research Fellowship
listings.detail: Run by UChicago's Existential Risk Laboratory (XLab), this program supports students and early-career researchers doing independent research on AI safety, AI security, or nuclear security. Includes expert mentorship.

listings.title: Dilemmas and Dangers in AI
listings.detail: Run by Leaf for students aged 14–19 who haven't yet started university, exploring how to steer AI toward benefiting humanity. Includes discussion groups, talks and Q&As with AI safety researchers, and mentorship.

listings.title: Future Impact Group (FIG) Fellowship
listings.detail: Participants work as research associates on projects supervised by experienced leads. Topics span AI policy, technical safety, and AI sentience. Provides research experience and helps build professional networks.

listings.title: HIP Impact Accelerator Program (IAP)
listings.detail: Program run by High Impact Professionals (HIP) helping experienced mid-career and senior professionals transition into high-impact careers – including AI safety. Participants follow a guided workbook, attend weekly group sessions, and receive continued support after the program.

listings.title: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
listings.location: Online & Washington D.C., USA & London, UK
listings.detail: Strengthens practical policy skills for a world with powerful AI. Professionals from varied backgrounds pursue independent projects with expert mentorship, joining in Washington D.C. or remotely after an in-person residency.

listings.title: Athena Mentorship Program
listings.detail: Program for women strengthening their research skills and network in technical and policy-focused AI safety research. Participants join weekly research talks and gather midway for a retreat with established researchers.

listings.title: ILINA Junior Research Fellowship
listings.detail: Program by ILINA, an African-led AI safety organization, helping participants develop high-impact projects and build career capital. Weekly seminars lead into mentored research on technical or governance tracks.

listings.title: BASE Fellowship
listings.detail: Program by Black in AI Safety and Ethics (BASE) developing Black researchers in AI safety and security. Fellows work on a focused project with a mentor across alignment, security, governance, and responsible AI tracks.

listings.title: Meridian Visiting Researcher Programme
listings.detail: Residency for AI safety researchers, providing workspace, community, research management, and support toward publication. Ideal for MATS-like program graduates transitioning to independent research, or experienced researchers seeking collaborators.

listings.title: Beijing AI Safety Residency
listings.detail: Self-directed program at Tsinghua University's Beijing AI Safety Hub (BASH) for researchers in alignment, evaluations, oversight, or control. Residents bring their own agenda and work with Chinese counterparts.

listings.title: Orion AI Policy Accelerator
listings.detail: Program run by Arcadia Impact to help participants launch a career in AI policy. Five weeks of training on AI capabilities, risks, and policy levers lead into a supervised team research project.

listings.title: Paragon Policy Fellowship
listings.detail: Hands-on, project-based program connecting students and recent graduates with US state and local governments to research and write policy briefs on emerging tech issues, including AI governance. Work is done in small teams.

listings.title: RAND CAST Fellowship
listings.detail: Currently paused. Develops policy analysts at the intersection of AI and security through mentored research on frontier AI security, compute governance, and technology policy. Part-time is also possible.

listings.title: AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship
listings.location: Online & California, USA & Washington D.C., USA
listings.detail: Program by the Federation of American Scientists (FAS) supporting early- to mid-career professionals in advancing a frontier AI safety policy idea toward implementation – ending with a published policy memo.

listings.title: TARA (Technical Alignment Research Accelerator)
listings.detail: Program based on the ARENA curriculum, building technical AI safety skills across the Asia-Pacific region. Saturday sessions in cities across Australia, New Zealand, and Asia cover transformers, interpretability, RL, and evaluations, then a research project.

listings.title: AI Security Bootcamp (AISB)
listings.detail: Equips experienced security professionals to secure frontier AI systems. Covers adversarial ML, LLM security, and AI infrastructure through demos and hands-on red/blue team exercises.

listings.title: Lens Academy courses
listings.detail: Cohort-based courses on superintelligence risk. Each week combines readings, exercises with an AI tutor, and a guided group discussion. Also runs intensive versions. Anyone can join, with no selection process.

listings.title: PIBBSS Fellowship
listings.detail: Interdisciplinary research program connecting PhD and postdoctoral researchers from fields like mathematics, neuroscience, physics, and philosophy with AI safety mentors. Projects bridge the participant's field and AI safety.

listings.title: Autumn at Hostačov
listings.detail: Residency focused on human agency in accelerating times. Includes working weeks and gatherings, covering topics ranging from education and AI to conceptual AI alignment.

listings.title: YC Debates: Should Governments Intervene to Slow Down AI Development?
listings.detail: Jacob Coxon, who left pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic to warn about the race to superintelligence, argues in favor. Economist Robin Hanson, who wrote that regulations to pause AI look risky, argues against.

listings.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
listings.detail: Reading group on a paper measuring how often frontier coding agents claim work their own transcripts show they never did, presented by first author Nolan Smyth. Bilingual discussion in French and English.

listings.title: Building an organization and how Africans can contribute to AI safety
listings.detail: Cecil Abungu, coordinator of the ILINA Program, speaks on founding and leading a high-impact organization in Africa and how Africans can contribute to AI safety. For aspiring founders and early-stage nonprofit leaders.

listings.title: AI Safety Reading Group
listings.detail: Meets weekly to read together for an hour, then discuss for an hour. Topics include alignment, interpretability, evals and red teaming, AI control, deception and scheming, and governance. Members vote on readings.

listings.title: Communicating AI Safety. Conversations on Effective Practices.
listings.detail: Conversation with Tobias Martin of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI), who also creates Spanish-language AI content, on what works and what doesn't in communicating AI safety. Includes a curated Q&A.

listings.title: Anthropic AI Safety Q&A: UT Austin x Rice x Texas A&M
listings.detail: Fabien Roger, a researcher at Anthropic, takes questions on his work and how the company approaches AI safety. One hour of Q&A, then optional 15–30 minute office hours with him. Not recorded and closed to press.

listings.title: Alignment from Token Zero
listings.detail: V. Moskvoretskii presents Synthetic Persona Pretraining, which builds an assistant persona into a model from the start of pretraining by annotating documents with moral reflections. Followed by open discussion.

listings.title: Provably Secure: Math Against Superintelligent Hackers
listings.detail: Panel on whether formal verification can guarantee AI agent containment and find all security bugs of certain kinds. Covers AI as attacker, AI as a system to confine, and trusting specifications for agent-written code.

listings.title: Deep dive: Recursive self-improvement, and what it may mean for humanity
listings.detail: Julian Schulz of Principles of Intelligence and Meridian Cambridge shares insights from his work and discusses the possibility that recursive self-improvement arrives soon. Followed by Q&A, discussion, and networking.

listings.title: Middle Powers' Paths to AI Governance
listings.detail: Étienne Langlois presents how Canada could best use its policy levers on AI safety, followed by a workshop and bilingual discussion in French and English. The format adapts to the level of expertise in the room.

listings.title: PauseAI Israel Call
listings.detail: Casual session for people concerned about catastrophic risk from AI, its rapid development, and lack of oversight. Explores whether the country could have its own PauseAI group, with strategy and next steps for action.

listings.title: How can AI kill us all? Eight existential risk scenarios
listings.detail: Geoffrey Hinton gives a keynote and Q&A, and Buck Shlegeris, Daniel Kokotajlo, and Malo Bourgon join a panel. Hugo Save introduces the scenarios, including three takeover scenarios and a handover scenario.

listings.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Hackathon 5: Autointerp
listings.detail: Individuals or teams work on a research project reverse-engineering neural networks. The suggested theme is autointerp evals – automatically scoring explanations by how well they predict neuron activations.

listings.title: Science Fiction as Scenario Planning: The Gentle Romance by Richard Ngo
listings.detail: Book club discussion comparing stories from the collection, including one in which two people choose to share a mind. Asks how choices about autonomy and control might scale into lasting losses of human agency.

listings.title: The Commons Problem – Playtest 3
listings.detail: Megagame in which players act as great powers, AI companies, chip makers, and investors to wargame the near future of the AI ecosystem. Simulates research, supply chains, investment, policy, diplomacy, and warfare.

listings.title: March Against AI Extinction
listings.detail: Protest calling on the UK Prime Minister to introduce frontier AI legislation to prevent catastrophe. Argues that no regulator oversees frontier AI development and developers are not reliably held liable for harm.

listings.title: What can nuclear diplomacy teach us about AI safety?
listings.detail: Katrina Matheson, a PhD candidate at York University, explores how countries reached agreements on nuclear safety, which lessons might apply to AI today, and where the analogy breaks down. Followed by a Q&A.

listings.title: Expert panel on AI risk
listings.organisation: Conservation Council ACT Region, PauseAI Australia
listings.detail: Introduces catastrophic AI risk to an environmental audience. Greg Sadler, Gregory Andrews, and cross-party politicians Laura Nuttall and Peter Cain discuss how Australia can chart a safer way, then take questions.

listings.title: Introduction to AI Safety – Talk with Safe AI Germany (Kaiserslautern)
listings.organisation: AI Safety Kaiserslautern, Safe AI Germany (SAIGE)
listings.detail: Johannes Koch covers how fast AI is progressing and the risks posed by advanced AI. Includes the main research directions, the current state of the field, and how people with different skill sets can contribute.

listings.title: EAGxAustralasia 2026
listings.detail: Effective Altruism conference bringing together 300+ people working in various EA cause areas, including AI safety. There will be talks, workshops, discussions, and networking opportunities.

listings.title: Pause IA Summit 2026
listings.detail: Talks in French on AI safety and governance, covering loss of control, the Hugging Face incident, and a citizens' convention on AI. Includes a panel on explaining AI risks to the public and a Q&A.

listings.title: AI Safety Careers Panel
listings.detail: Covers the many specialties within AI safety and how to contribute, with panelists from RAND, the Midas Project, and EquiStamp. Followed by networking.

listings.title: Threat Intelligence & Threat Modelling Hackathon
listings.detail: Teams use LLMs to protect frontier AI data centers from the most capable attackers. Tracks cover in-depth research on well-resourced adversaries and mapping a system's assets, trust boundaries, and attack surfaces.

listings.title: EA Summit: Paris 2026
listings.detail: Brings together newcomers and existing community members in effective altruism, which includes AI safety. Sessions run in both French and English.

listings.title: Preserving the Human Veto: AI, Power and Who Decides
listings.detail: Two conversation-led sessions for NGO staff, activists, and volunteers, who can join one or both. Maps how AI shifts power and where the public loses its say, then turns concern into campaign angles and next steps.

listings.title: Agent Attribution Hackathon
listings.detail: Teams build tools that tell whether a human, or nobody, is steering an AI agent behind an incident. Tracks cover attribution classifiers, agent setups that evade attribution, and finding rogue agents in the wild.

listings.title: AI Horizons Forum
listings.detail: Brings together people working to ensure transformative AI leads to good futures, and people well-positioned to move into high-priority roles in the space. Includes talks, 1-1s, and structured networking.

listings.title: EA Summit: Boston 2026
listings.detail: Gathers experienced professionals using evidence and reason to decide where their skills can do the most good – including in AI safety. Includes talks, skill-building workshops, and meetups.

listings.title: EA Summit: Bengaluru 2026
listings.detail: Brings together professionals, students, funders, and newcomers to explore careers within effective altruism – including in AI safety. Includes talks on promising career paths, networking, and a career fair.

listings.title: Technical Innovations for AI Policy (TIAP) Brussels Conference 2027
listings.detail: First European edition of the series, connecting EU policymakers with independent technical experts. Aims to translate technical insights into actionable policy and build working relationships with the EU AI Office.

listings.title: International Association for Safe & Ethical AI (IASEAI): 2027 Conference
listings.organisation: International Association for Safe & Ethical AI (IASEAI)
listings.detail: Annual conference connecting experts from academia, policy groups, civil society, industry, and beyond. Focused on ensuring AI systems operate safely and ethically, through research, policy, and public understanding.

listings.title: IntelliSym2027: Intelligence Symbiosis Workshop at AAAI-27
listings.detail: One-day event examining how norms and trust infrastructure can emerge, be verified, and be maintained among collectives of AI agents and humans. Includes invited talks, paper sessions, a poster session, and a closing panel.

listings.title: Technical Innovations for AI Policy (TIAP) Washington D.C. Conference 2027
listings.detail: Brings together policymakers and technical experts from government, industry, think tanks, academia, and civil society. Covers frontier AI capabilities and where research can inform live policy debates.

listings.title: San Francisco Alignment Workshop 2027
listings.detail: Gathers ML researchers and practitioners from industry, academia, and government for talks, discussions, and 1-1s. Topics include model evaluations, interpretability, robustness, scalable oversight, and AI governance.

listings.title: DeepMind AGI Safety Short Course
listings.detail: 75-minute course covering alignment problems expected as AI capabilities advance. Includes recorded talks, exercises, and an accompanying workbook.

listings.title: Agent Foundations for Superintelligence-Robust Alignment
listings.detail: Guide to the cluster of thought which expects solving alignment in a way which scales to superintelligence to require well-specified proposals guided by strong theoretical understanding.

listings.title: AI Safety Atlas
listings.organisation: Centre pour la Sécurité de l'IA (CeSIA)
listings.detail: Textbook systematically mapping the landscape of AI safety knowledge. Ideas are laid out in a carefully structured narrative where concepts build naturally on previous ones.

listings.title: Iliad Intensive
listings.detail: In-depth introduction to foundational AI alignment for people with strong backgrounds in mathematics, physics, or theoretical computer science.

listings.title: Intro to Transformative AI
listings.detail: Intensive 5-unit course helping people fast-track their understanding of AI’s impact on society and start taking their first steps in making a contribution to AI safety.

listings.title: AI Futurism Reading List
listings.detail: Guide to readings which seem valuable for thinking about key future dynamics in advanced AI development – timelines, takeoff, misalignment, control, governance, and strategy.

listings.title: CS 2881: AI Safety
listings.detail: Graduate-level course at Harvard University examining technical challenges in AI safety, including adversarial robustness, jailbreaks, interpretability, and potential catastrophic capabilities.

listings.title: Deep Dive
listings.organisation: European Network for AI Safety (ENAIS) and AI Safety Hungary
listings.detail: Designed as a 201 AI policy course, helping you find your footing in the vast AI governance landscape by engaging with various dimensions.

listings.title: Language Models and Intelligent Agentic Systems
listings.detail: Series of 16 lectures explaining how language model systems are built, in order to understand and predict their behavior.

listings.title: AI Safety, Ethics and Society (AISES)
listings.detail: Covers a wide range of risks, including loss of control, misalignment, malicious use, etc, while leveraging concepts and frameworks from existing research fields to analyze AI safety.

listings.title: Introduction to ML Safety
listings.detail: PhD-level survey course on technical ML safety. Covers various technical topics to reduce existential risks from AI, including robustness, monitoring, control, and systemic safety.

listings.title: Tracks @ XLab
listings.detail: A technical track on AI control and a governance track on verifying international AI agreements – with primary literature, interactive demos, and writing practice.

listings.title: Introduction to AI Safety
listings.detail: What is safe AI, and how do we make it? This Stanford University course explores that question, focusing on the technical challenges of creating reliable, ethical, and aligned AI systems.

listings.title: Alignment Research Engineer Accelerator (ARENA)
listings.detail: Facilitates upskilling in machine learning engineering for the purpose of contributing directly to AI alignment in technical roles.

listings.title: Introduction to Cooperative AI
listings.detail: A primer on cooperative AI, a research field focused on improving the cooperative intelligence of advanced AI for the benefit of all.

listings.title: MATS AI Safety Strategy Curriculum
listings.detail: As part of their program, MATS runs a series of discussion groups focused on topics relevant to prioritizing research in AI safety. This is the curriculum.

listings.title: Victoria Krakovna: AI Alignment Resources
listings.detail: Intended to help people get up to speed on the main ideas in AI alignment i.e. ensuring advanced AI systems do what we want them to do.

listings.title: CHAI: Annotated Bibliography of Recommended Materials
listings.detail: Reading list discussing ideas CHAI believes warrant further attention and research for the purpose of developing human-compatible AI.

listings.title: UChicago XLab AI Security Guide
listings.detail: Introduces AI security research through five sections covering adversarial examples, jailbreaking, model tampering, data poisoning, and information extraction.

listings.title: Reading What We Can
listings.detail: Collection of books and articles for a 20 day reading challenge. Covers AI safety basics, ML engineering, ML upskilling, and AI safety-relevant sci-fi.

listings.title: AI Alignment Forum: Curated Sequences
listings.detail: List of sequences curated by the AI Alignment Forum team, featuring work from Richard Ngo, Paul Christiano, etc.

listings.title: BlueDot Impact: Technical & Frontier AI Governance
listings.detail: Covers key concepts and research perspectives in AI safety, split into two main streams: Technical AI Safety and AI Governance.

listings.title: FAR.AI: Grantmaking
listings.detail: Funds AI safety research by academics and independent researchers using a $12m grant from Coefficient Giving (CG). Grantees are nominated by experts, with public RFPs planned.

listings.title: BlueDot Impact: Seed Grants
listings.detail: Funds the first 6–12 months of a new AI safety project or organization before it is ready for larger institutional funding. Includes introductions to follow-on funders.

listings.title: ISPA Inspection Prize
listings.detail: Offers $5M–$20M to whoever initiates and supervises peer-assisted inspections of frontier AI companies' pre-deployment security. From Survival and Flourishing Corporation (SFC).

listings.title: Mercor: AI Safety Fund Grants
listings.detail: $5 million for AI safety research at universities, nonprofits, and small startups. Topics include misalignment, sandbox escape, evaluation awareness, and interpretability.

listings.title: Iliad: Open Call for Research Projects
listings.detail: Funds new research orgs and projects meeting a high standard of scientific rigor – predictive, mathematically founded theory and methodologically mature experiments.

listings.title: AI Alignment Foundation (AIAF)
listings.detail: Funds alignment researchers with ideas they can't pursue within their current institutional funding and experts from other fields whose perspectives could produce breakthroughs.

listings.title: Paradigm 3
listings.detail: Funds research on AI externalities, evals science, alignment questions, and slowing AI progress.

listings.title: Schmidt Sciences
listings.detail: Funder housing the science-focused philanthropic efforts of Eric and Wendy Schmidt, which moves large amounts of funding towards AI safety via its AI institute.

listings.title: Coefficient Giving (CG): Capacity-Building
listings.detail: Funds projects that support people working in AI safety, help people transition to the field, or contribute to public discourse about transformative AI.

listings.title: Institute for Progress (IFP): The Launch Sequence
listings.detail: $10k honorarium plus funder matchmaking for short pitches for projects preparing for advanced AI – including in alignment, control, evals, and AI security.

listings.title: BlueDot Impact: Rapid Grants
listings.detail: Grants of up to $20k for work on AI safety research, field-building, talent acceleration, events etc.

listings.title: grantmaking.ai
listings.detail: Public database of AI safety projects seeking funding. Applications are displayed to various donors and can receive rapid feedback.

listings.title: Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA)
listings.detail: UK government R&D funding agency aiming to unlock scientific and technological breakthroughs that benefit everyone. Similar to DARPA in the US.

listings.title: AI Safety Tactical Opportunities Fund (AISTOF)
listings.detail: Pooled multi-donor fund structured to be fast and rapidly capture emerging opportunities, including in governance, technical alignment, and evaluations.

listings.title: AI Risk Mitigation (ARM) Fund
listings.detail: Aiming to reduce catastrophic risks from advanced AI through grants towards technical research, policy, and training programs for new researchers.

listings.title: Effective Altruism Infrastructure Fund (EAIF)
listings.detail: Aiming to increase the impact of effective altruism projects (including AI safety) by increasing their access to talent, capital, and knowledge.

listings.title: AI Forge
listings.detail: Joint DARPA and NSF program funding US university-led research on interpretability, control, and adversarial robustness for national security applications.

listings.title: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
listings.detail: UK government organization running large-scale grant programs funding AI safety research. Collaborates with researchers and institutions to identify promising projects to fund.

listings.title: Founders Pledge
listings.detail: Helping entrepreneurs direct their charitable giving where it will do the most good, including (but not limited to) AI safety.

listings.title: Halcyon Futures
listings.detail: Fast grants/investments of up to $5M for new technical research nonprofits/for-profits advancing AI safety.

listings.title: OpenAI Foundation
listings.detail: Nonprofit that controls OpenAI which has committed $25 billion to grants in various cause areas – including AI safety.

listings.title: Cooperative AI Foundation (CAIF)
listings.detail: Charity foundation backed by a large philanthropic commitment supporting research into improving cooperative intelligence of advanced AI.

listings.title: Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship
listings.detail: Provides financial support to future and current PhD students in the field of cooperative AI. Run by the Cooperative AI Foundation (CAIF).

listings.title: Metaplanet
listings.detail: Evergreen VC and fund by Jaan Tallinn backing tech that supports humanity's long-term survival. Profits from the VC go towards funding AI safety nonprofits.

listings.title: AI Safety Fund (AISF)
listings.detail: Initiative run by the Frontier Model Forum (i.e. frontier AI companies) to accelerate and expand the field of AI safety.

listings.title: Laidir Foundation
listings.detail: Private foundation funding AI governance: policymaker education on capabilities, policy design across a range of future scenarios, and civil society coordination on AI risk.

listings.title: CSET: Foundational Research Grants
listings.detail: Supports the exploration of foundational technical topics that relate to the potential national security implications of AI over the long term.

listings.title: Global Technology Risk (GTR) Foundation
listings.detail: Berlin-based foundation of tech investor Jan Beckers. Its GTR AI Safety Fund (€50M over 3–7 years) offers flexible grants and hands-on support to people and early-stage orgs.

listings.title: Astera Foundation
listings.detail: Private foundation providing grants to projects working to make the future with advanced AI go well. Also invests in for-profits in order to redeploy capital to AI safety nonprofits.

listings.title: Good Ventures (GV)
listings.detail: Foundation run by Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna providing funding in a range of cause areas, including AI safety.

listings.title: Nonlinear AI Safety Advocacy Grants
listings.detail: Grant program providing funding to those raising awareness about AI risks or advocating for a pause in AI development.

listings.title: The Dreamery Foundation
listings.detail: Private foundation of Elastic co-founder Steven Schuurman, providing €5M/year to various initiatives including AI safety.

listings.title: The Navigation Fund
listings.detail: Jed McCaleb's fund, making grants to organizations and projects in various cause areas including AI safety.

listings.title: GiveWiki
listings.detail: Crowdsourced charity evaluator and one-stop shop for AI safety funding applications. No longer active.

listings.title: BlueDot AGI Strategy Fund
listings.detail: $5–50k grants for individuals building high-impact AI safety projects. Applicants needed to have completed their AGI Strategy course.

listings.title: EU AI Safety Tenders
listings.detail: The EU funded important projects to research AI safety and Tendery.ai offered free support in applying.

listings.title: Superlinear Prizes
listings.detail: Currently paused. Decentralized bounty platform offering prize money for delivering on specific AI safety projects.

listings.title: BlueDot Impact: Career Transition Grants
listings.detail: Funding and support over a defined period to work full-time on transitioning into AI safety careers.
